newsitem.title: USA: Entergy says three 500 kv lines still down.
newsitem.headline: Entergy says three 500 kv lines still down.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Monday three of its 500 kilovolt (kv) Arkansas transmission lines are still out of service following a band of 20 tornadoes that initially wiped out service to 18,000 customers a week ago.
"Two of those (lines) are in heavily flooded areas, so our crews are having a tough time getting in there," company spokeswoman Carol Copeland said.
"We also have three 161 or 115 kv lines still down," she added.
"Everyone that can accept power has power," she said, noting full restoration of power to those customers was met last Wednesday.

Last week, Entergy reported that the severe weather on March 1 damaged or destroyed 36 steel towers supporting five of its 500 kv lines. Six 161 kv lines and four 115 kv lines were also struck down by the tornadoes.
The company said it could take another couple of weeks to restore all damaged transmission lines.

New Orleans-based Entergy maintains about 119,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in its service territory, which covers parts of Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi and eastern Texas. It serves about 611,000 customers.
